alt: A transverse wave drawn against a dashed rest position, with crests and a trough marked. The wavelength is the distance between neighbouring crests and the amplitude is from the rest position to a crest. Below, straight wavefronts seen from above are one wavelength apart.
caption: Wavelength is crest to neighbouring crest; amplitude is rest position to crest.

alt: Ten wavefronts span 18 cm with nine gaps between them, so λ = 2.0 cm = 0.020 m and, at 12 Hz, v = 12 × 0.020 = 0.24 m/s. Other examples: sound at 340 m/s and 680 Hz has λ = 0.50 m; radio of λ 3.0 m has f = 1.0 × 10⁸ Hz; water waves of 0.25 Hz and 20 m travel at 5.0 m/s.
caption: n wavefronts have n − 1 gaps; then v = fλ in m, Hz and m/s.

alt: A transverse wave on a rope: each point vibrates up and down, at right angles to the direction the wave travels; examples are electromagnetic radiation, water waves and seismic S-waves. A longitudinal wave on a spring: each coil vibrates back and forth along the direction of travel; examples are sound and seismic P-waves.
caption: Transverse: vibration across the direction of travel. Longitudinal: along it.

alt: Left: straight wavefronts hit a plane barrier and reflect at the same angle on the other side of the normal, with speed, wavelength and frequency unchanged. Right: wavefronts entering shallower water slow down, so they are closer together and change direction; the frequency stays the same. At 12 Hz the wavelength is 2.0 cm in deep water (0.24 m/s) and 1.5 cm in shallow water (0.18 m/s).
caption: Reflection changes only direction; refraction changes speed and wavelength, not frequency.

alt: Three plan views of straight water wavefronts. Through a gap about one wavelength wide they spread into nearly semicircular wavefronts. Through a gap much wider than the wavelength they pass mostly straight with slight spreading at the edges. Past a single edge they curve round into the shadow region. The spacing of the wavefronts stays the same.
caption: Diffraction is greatest when the gap is about the size of the wavelength.
